newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police detain 21 after neo-Nazi attacks.
newsitem.headline: German police detain 21 after neo-Nazi attacks.

text.p: German police said on Friday they had detained 21 people after right-wing extremists went on the rampage across eastern Germany the previous day.
Fourteen people were injured as violence broke out in towns across East Germany on Thursday's Ascension Day public holiday, police said.

One person was hurt when around 20 drunken thugs chanted Nazi slogans and threw stones and fenceposts at a refugee home in the small town of Gnaschwitz in Saxony. Police detained eight suspected attackers there.
Extremists hurled a firebomb at another refugee home in the Saxon town of Groeditz and threatened residents there.
Eight people were injured in Magdeburg when thugs armed with chains stormed a meeting of amateur radio operators in the early hours of Friday. Eight suspects were detained.
In Gera, south of Leipzig, police detained 13 people and said two left-wingers and three police were injured after a fight broke out between right-wing extremists and left-wingers.

Police in the western town of Kaiserslautern said unknown assailants had desecrated a Jewish graveyard by overturning 25 gravestones and defacing 65 with swastikas and anti-Semitic abuse in red paint.

Germany witnessed a rise in right-wing violence after unification in 1990, particularly in the former communist east. Commentators fear that record post-war unemployment -- 4.35 million in April -- is sparking a new surge in extremism.
